title: Budget horizon sampler and compact-quant regulator for tenant defaults
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware budget horizon sampler that synthesizes sliding-window unit-econ signals and a compact-quant regulator that recommends conservative quant profiles as safe defaults. Non-breaking; improves cost defaults and reduces tail spend for small/medium tenants.
description:
Context and motivation: We observe that many small-to-mid tenants keep conservative defaults that either overprovision GPU time (high token cost) or opt for aggressive quant profiles that cause quality regressions. Existing heuristics are static per-tenant and do not account for temporal spend patterns (seasonality, bursts). This PR introduces a Budget Horizon Sampler service that synthesizes sliding-window unit-economics signals (horizon-aware smoothing) and a Compact-Quant Regulator that maps those signals to conservative default recommendations for batching, cache retention, and quantization tier.

What this change delivers: 1) A horizon sampler that computes a 7/14/30-day budget curve per tenant using weighted decays and tail-smoothing; 2) A regulator that converts horizon curves into a recommended defaults payload (batch_size_hint, cache_ttl_hint, quant_profile_tag) with safety floors and rollback markers; 3) A CLI and admin endpoint to preview recommendations and run dry-runs; 4) Integration into Defaults Propagator so tenant defaults are updated via opt-in rollout.

Checklist (high level): - [x] Horizon sampler implementation (pkg/econ/horizon) - [x] Compact-quant regulator service and policy table (pkg/econ/regulator) - [x] Defaults propagation hook & opt-in rollout (services/defaults-propagator) - [x] CLI (cmd/rh-budget-preview) and simple dry-run mode - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Performance smoke tests - [x] Docs: admin short-runbook and API schema notes

Commits summary: * 1/3 - add horizon sampler core algorithm and unit tests (weighted-window, tail-smoother) * 2/3 - add compact-quant regulator, policy table, and mapping tests (safety floors) * 3/3 - hook into defaults-propagator, add CLI preview, integration tests, docs and telemetry metrics (horizon.sampled, regulator.recommendation.count)

Changed areas (high level, illustrative snippets): - pkg/econ/horizon/horizon.go: adds SlidingWindowSampler and associated smoothing utilities (approx. 320 LOC). Example snippet: func SlidingWindowSampler(events []Event, windowDays int) HorizonCurve { /* weighted-decay + tail-smooth */ } - pkg/econ/regulator/regulator.go: policy table, compact quant mapping rules, and safety floor logic. Snippet: func Recommend(profile HorizonCurve) Recommendation { /* map to batch/cache/quant */ } - services/defaults-propagator/handler.go: opt-in rollout hook that accepts Recommendation and emits a staged update event (no immediate override). - cmd/rh-budget-preview/main.go: small CLI to fetch tenant curve + regulator output for manual review. - docs/admin/budget-horizon.md: short runbook and rollout guidance. - telemetry/metrics.yaml: add horizon.sampled, regulator.recommendation.count, regulator.rollback.invoked. - tests/integration/horizon_regulator_test.go: end-to-end dry-run assertions.

Review conversation (selected): Diego Martinez (reviewer): "Algorithm looks sensible; two requests: (1) add a brief note in the code linking the weighted-decay constants to the empirical study you ran, and (2) ensure the regulator never suggests quant profiles below our 'safe-quant' minimum for latency-sensitive classes."\nAuthor (Ava): "Added comments pointing to the mini-experiment (tools/benchmarks/horizon-walk/README.md) and enforced a quant floor in regulator.go; see commit 2/3."\nPriya Kapoor (reviewer): "Integration tests flaked initially on CI because defaults-propagator expected the older API. Suggest adding a compatibility shim and a feature flag for rollout."\nAuthor: "Added backward-compatible shim and a feature flag RELEASE_BUDGET_HORIZON_ROLLOUT, default off for canary. Integration tests updated; CI rerun passed."\nMarcus Liu (approver): "Perf smoke looks fine; recommend a gradual canary to 5% tenants. Approving.",

CI summary and checks: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass (horizon unit tests added) - integration-tests: originally failed on compatibility; fixed and passed on rerun - lint: pass (minor style fix) - perf-smoke: pass (latency uplift < 1% p50) - canary-sim: pass (simulated 1k tenant run with recommended defaults showed estimated 12-18% tail spend reduction for small tenants)

Safety and rollout notes: The regulator includes hard safety floors (min_batch_size=1, min_cache_ttl_seconds=30, safe_quant_min_tag=\"q8_anon\") and an automatic rollback marker emitted if observed error-rate or eval-quality drift crosses thresholds. Defaults-propagator applies recommendations only for tenants with opt-in flag or during controlled canary (admin-controlled percentage).

Telemetry and observability: New metrics (horizon.sampled, regulator.recommendation.count, regulator.applied.count, regulator.rollback.count) and a tracing span around the regulator decision path were added. Alerts suggested in docs/admin/budget-horizon.md: alert if regulator.rollback.count > 1% in 24h window.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Post-merge tasks: schedule a 2-week canary with telemetry dashboard (assigned to Priya), add a Linear ticket for tenant UX to opt-in prompts (PM-900).
